description: CAD bake-off 1 of 3 -- OPENSCAD: build the SO-101 gripper assembly parametrically in cad/openscad/. SHARED CONTEXT (same task, three tools, one pebble each so they can run in separate git worktrees): recreate the SO-101 gripper assembly -- the fixed jaw (gripper body) and the moving jaw -- as a baseline for comparing three CAD tools. Jake verbatim: "I want to be able to modify them in the future, so you will have to do it in a way that supports that." That means parametric, editable source. Importing a mesh and calling it done FAILS the test. Use named variables for every dimension that might plausibly change: jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes, wall thickness. DIMENSIONAL SOURCE OF TRUTH -- two real SO-101 STEP files are already committed at cad/build123d/reference/: Moving_Jaw_SO101.step and Wrist_Roll_Follower_SO101.step. STEP carries exact analytic geometry, so measure from these. Do NOT re-download them and do NOT invent or eyeball dimensions from tessellated meshes. WHY THIS PART: it is what Jake will modify for the Hand 1.0 paper gripper -- cross-reference plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md as reading, and cite them in your notes. DELIVERABLE BESIDES THE MODEL: a NOTES.md in your own tool directory covering time taken, what was easy, what was painful, whether the tool known weakness actually mattered in practice, and how it would feel to modify this part six months from now. State plainly if the geometry ends up approximate and list what still needs verifying. BOUNDARIES: stay inside your own cad/<tool>/ directory and touch nothing else. Do NOT edit plans/hand_1_0.md or plans/gripper_bet.md -- a later pass writes the comparison across all three tools. The other two tool pebbles are running in parallel in their own worktrees, so do not touch cad/openscad/, cad/build123d/, or cad/blender/ other than your own. TOOL SPECIFICS: OpenSCAD is installed at /Applications/OpenSCAD.app; the CLI binary is inside the bundle at /Applications/OpenSCAD.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenSCAD. Write .scad source with a named-variable block at the top. Prove it compiles by rendering a PNG and exporting an STL from the CLI, both committed. Note the reference STEP files live under cad/build123d/reference/ -- read them for dimensions only (OpenSCAD cannot import STEP, so measure and transcribe), and write nothing into that directory. KNOWN LIMITATION TO EVALUATE HONESTLY IN NOTES.md: OpenSCAD is mesh output only -- no B-rep, no true fillets, no STEP export. Does that actually bite on THIS part, or is it irrelevant here? Give a real verdict, not a hedge. The upside to weigh against it: a single self-contained file with no dependencies.
test_instructions: cad/openscad/ contains parametric .scad source with a named-variable block covering jaw length, jaw opening, fingertip thickness, servo horn bore, fastener sizes and wall thickness
A PNG render and an STL export produced by /Applications/OpenSCAD.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenSCAD are committed
cad/openscad/NOTES.md covers time, easy, painful, whether the no-B-rep/no-fillet/no-STEP limitation mattered on this part, six-month modifiability, and what still needs verifying
Nothing outside cad/openscad/ is modified -- in particular plans/hand_1_0.md and plans/gripper_bet.md are untouched
